draft.title: The Sustainable Development Goals
card: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are 17 goals set by the United Nations. All UN member countries agreed to them in 2015.
The goals aim to be reached by 2030. They are part of a plan called the 2030 Agenda.
The goals cover many issues, including poverty, health, education, inequality, climate change and the environment.
The goals are linked. Progress on one, such as education, can help with others, such as reducing poverty. They are shared aims, not laws that force countries to act.
draft.remember: The SDGs are 17 shared, linked goals for 2030, covering issues from poverty to the environment.

a.q: Which option best describes the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
opts: 17 goals agreed by UN members in 2015, aimed at 2030
17 laws that the UN enforces on each member country
8 goals agreed in 2000, aimed at ending hunger only
17 goals that deal only with climate and the environment
a.why: The SDGs are 17 goals agreed in 2015 with a target date of 2030. The option about climate only is tempting, but the goals also cover poverty, health, education and inequality.
a.clue: Think about the number of goals, the year they were agreed and their range.

b.q: A community program in Shepparton, Victoria, helps girls from low-income families stay in school. Over time, their families' incomes rise. What does this show about the SDGs?
opts: The goals are linked, so progress on one can help another
The goals are separate, so each must be met on its own
The goals are laws, so schools must follow them
The goals cover only the environment, not people
b.why: Better education led to higher incomes, so progress on an education goal helped with poverty. This shows the goals are linked. The option about separate goals is tempting, but the card says progress on one can help others.
b.clue: Look at how one change led to another.

a.best: 17 goals agreed by UN members in 2015, aimed at 2030

b.best: The goals are linked, so progress on one can help another
